_comment: Mutation testing on the money paths (audit item B22, 2026-08-16). Stryker is NOT a devDependency on purpose — HetCreep's call: it is a measuring tool run occasionally, and installing it costs 195 packages and 2 moderate advisories in a repo that otherwise carries zero. `npm run test:mutation` invokes it through npx at a pinned version instead. NOT wired into `npm run ci`: 30 minutes per run, and there is no threshold to gate on yet.
_baseline: Run 2, 2026-08-17, 1128 mutants, 21m00s: overall 75.35% (743 killed, 107 timed out, 180 survived, 98 no-coverage). Per file — combatSummary 100.00 · stageRewardConfig 100.00 · rewardValidator 98.65 · gachaConfig 97.53 · rewardConfig 96.23 · lobbyBattleRewardPipeline 88.00 · stageRewardResolver 72.13 · rewardProgress 66.67 · resultFinalizer 64.15 · rewardGrantService 53.54 · rewardResolver 43.04 · resultViewModel 31.82 · dungeonRewardPipeline 24.24.
_baseline_run1: Run 1, 2026-08-16, same 1128 mutants, 30m29s: overall 52.66% (517 killed, 77 timed out, 352 survived, 182 no-coverage). What it found, and what closing it cost: stageRewardConfig 31.86 with 154 SURVIVING mutants, gachaConfig 28.40 and combatSummary 5.71 with 84 lines no test reached at all — stage payouts and pull pricing, the values ECONOMY-DESIGN-LOCK.md governs. Three test files closed those in run 2. Kept here because a first measurement is the only one taken before anyone knew the number.
_read_the_score_honestly: stageRewardConfig reads 100.00 and that overstates what the tests detect. Stryker counts a TIMED-OUT mutant as killed, and 58 of that file's 226 mutants are timeouts, not assertion failures — mutating a module-level constant forces a full reload, which is slow rather than caught. The tests there assert invariants (item ids resolve, sourceIds are unique and match their stage, amounts are positive integers, the wave bonus multiplies per wave) and deliberately do NOT pin the individual payout numbers, because pinning them would freeze magic numbers against the base × scale rule the economy lock sets. So: changing trial-04's gold from 70 to 71 still would not fail a test. That is a deliberate trade, not an oversight — see the comment at the top of src/game/reward/stageRewardTable.test.ts.
_setup_notes: Two settings here are workarounds, not preferences. tsconfigFile points at a file that does not exist: Stryker 10 TSConfigPreprocessor calls ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson, which TypeScript 7 removed along with the rest of the config-parsing API, and it crashes the run — naming a tsconfig outside the project file set makes the preprocessor no-op instead. vitest.related is false because Stryker could not map mutants to tests, which then made the dry run the whole 1198-test suite and blew the 5-minute timeout; vitest.mutation.config.ts narrows it to the 11 files that touch these two folders.
_schema_note: No $schema key: it can only point at ./node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/schema/, and Stryker is not installed here (see _comment). A dangling $schema is worse than none — the editor reports a missing file on every open.
